proof_summary: Letting \(d=s(n)\) and \(e=s(d)\), the decimal congruence modulo \(9\) gives \(n=e+9q\); if \(q=0\), then \(d=n<10\) and \(10n\) is a partner. If \(q>0\), a digit-sum bound gives \(d<10^q\), and the proof uses the digitwise 9-complement of the zero-padded \(q\)-digit expansion of \(d-1\) to assemble a distinct positive \(k\) with \(s(k)=e+9q=n\) and \(d\mid k\), which supplies the required partner.
